name: Fury-Caldera
geological_features: Overlapping supervolcano calderas forming the entire surface
Rivers of molten sulfur cutting through basalt plains
Pyroclastic storm systems reaching the upper atmosphere
specific_features: Periodic synchronized eruptions suggesting subsurface resonance chambers
description: Fury-Caldera is a volcanic nightmare of overlapping supervolcano craters, each one feeding into the next in a chain of geological rage that has remade the planet's surface countless times over. Rivers of molten sulfur carve luminous yellow channels through fields of black basalt, and pyroclastic storms choke the sky with ash that glows ember-red from the reflected light below.

The toxic atmosphere is a choking blend of sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide, heated to temperatures that would cook unprotected flesh in minutes. The planet radiates anger, every eruption a scream, every lava flow a wound torn open and left to bleed.

Geological surveys revealed that the planet's eruptions follow a synchronized pattern, with calderas firing in sequence like chambers of a beating heart. Deep-core imaging suggests the existence of vast resonance chambers in the mantle that amplify and coordinate volcanic activity, a natural phenomenon that mimics engineered design with unsettling precision.

Despite the hostility, thermophilic microbial life thrives in the sulfur rivers, and the platinum deposits concentrated in cooled lava flows represent one of the richest mineral strikes in the sector. Automated mining operations have been attempted three times; all three ended when the machinery was consumed by eruptions that the resonance model failed to predict.
